fact: The DRC settled over $1.4m in arrears and penalties to the African Telecommunications Union, securing its automatic seat on the ATU Administrative Council; the document gives no date for the seat, so its published date is used.

The 7th ATU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abuja formally validated the move of the ATU headquarters from Nairobi to Kinshasa on 23 July 2026; the new Secretary-General is to take office there in January 2027.

The DRC is one of the seven member states of the East African Communications Organisation, and its regulator ARPTC submitted 2024-2025 data to EACO's regional statistics report; no event date is given, so the published date is used.

Kinshasa hosted the 10th Ordinary Session of ARTAC, the Conference of Central African Telecommunications Regulators, at which member states adopted a resolution mandating free roaming across Central Africa by 30 June 2026; the document gives no session date, so its published date is used.
Democratic Republic of the Congo sent a delegation to the fourth extraordinary session of the ARTAC regulators' conference held in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026, per GabonReview.
TechAfrika reports a delegation from The DRC attended the ARTAC session opened in Libreville on 20 October 2026.
The regulator of COD took part in the 4th extraordinary session of ARTAC in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026, per Tech Review Africa.
The regulator of COD took part in the 4th extraordinary session of ARTAC in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026, per ART Cameroon.

The DRC Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy signed an MoU with Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance on 11 May 2026 on digital transformation, connectivity, cybersecurity and digital skills, per Uganda's ministry.
Gabon and the DRC signed a mobile roaming agreement eliminating cross-border charges on the sidelines of ARTAC's 10th session in Kinshasa, reported by Ecofin Agency, taking effect 30 June 2026.
ART Cameroon says the DRC hosted ARTAC's 10th Ordinary Session in Kinshasa, 16-19 February 2026, and that its regulator ARPTC signed a roaming agreement with Gabon's ARCEP at the opening ceremony.
Ecofin Agency reports the country is one of ten countries selected for Smart Africa's IDECT project on digital payments and e-commerce policy.
ACP reports the DRC's ARPTC signed a roaming memorandum of understanding with Gabon's ARCEP on 19 February 2026 in Kinshasa, at the 10th ordinary session of the regulators' body ARTAC, held there.
